source_text: ΟΜΙΛΙΑ ΙΓʹ. Προτρεπτικὴ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον βάπτισμα. Ὁ μὲν σοφὸς Σολομὼν, τῶν κατὰ τὸν βίον πρα γμάτων τοὺς καιροὺς διαιρῶν, καὶ ἑκάστῳ τῶν γινο μένων τὸν ἐπιτήδειον ἀφορίζων, ἔφη· Τοῖς πᾶσιν ὁ χρόνος, καὶ καιρὸς τῷ παντὶ πράγματι· καιρὸς τοῦ τεκεῖν, καὶ καιρὸς τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν· ἐγὼ δὲ, μικρὸν τοῦ σοφοῦ τὴν ἀπόφασιν ὑπαλλάξας, εἴποιμι ἂν κηρύσσων ὑμῖν τὸ σωτήριον κήρυγμα, ὅτι καιρὸς τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν, καὶ καιρὸς τοῦ γεννηθῆναι. Τίς δὲ ὁ λό γος τῆς ἐναλλαγῆς; Ὅτι ὁ μὲν περὶ τῶν ἐν γενέσει καὶ φθορᾷ διαλεγόμενος, τῇ σωματικῇ ἑπόμε νος φύσει, τὴν γένεσιν προέταξε τοῦ θανάτου (ἀδύνα τον γὰρ θανάτου πεῖραν λαβεῖν τὸν μὴ πρότερον γεννηθέντα)· ἐγὼ δὲ, περὶ τῆς πνευματικῆς ἀναγεννήσεως τὸν λόγον ποιεῖσθαι μέλλων, τὸν θάνατον προτίθημι τῆς ζωῆς. Διὰ γὰρ τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν τῇ σαρκὶ περιγίνεται ἡμῖν τὸ γεννηθῆναι τῷ πνεύματι, καθά φησι καὶ ὁ Κύριος· Ἐγὼ ἀποκτενῶ, καὶ ζῇν ποιήσω. Ἀποθάνωμεν οὖν, ἵνα ζήσωμεν. Ἀποκτείνωμεν τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς, τὸ μὴ δυνάμενον ὑποταγῆναι τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ἰσχυρὸν ἡμῖν ἐγγένηται, δι' οὗ ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη περιγίνεσθαι πέφυκε. Συνταφῶμεν τῷ Χριστῷ τῷ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀποθανόντι, ἵνα καὶ συναναστῶμεν τῷ ἡμῖν τὴν ἀνάστασιν προξενήσαντι. Καιρὸς μὲν οὖν ἄλλοις ἄλλος ἐπιτήδειος· ἴδιος ὕπνου, καὶ ἴδιος ἐγρηγόρσεως· ἴδιος πολέμου, καὶ ἴδιος εἰρήνης· καιρὸς δὲ βαπτίσματος ἅπας ὁ τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίος. Οὔτε γὰρ σώματι ζῇν μὴ ἀνα πνέοντι δυνατὸν, οὔτε ψυχῇ συνεστάναι, μὴ γνωρι ζούσῃ τὸν κτίσαντα. Θεοῦ γὰρ ἄγνοια θάνατός ἐστι ψυχῆς. Ὁ δὲ μὴ βαπτισθεὶς οὐ πεφώτισται. Ἄνευ δὲ φωτὸς οὔτε ὀφθαλμὸς τὰ ἑαυτοῦ καθορᾷ, οὔτε ψυχὴ Θεοῦ δέξασθαι δύναται θεωρίαν. Πᾶς μὲν οὖν χρόνος εὐκαιρίαν ἔχει πρὸς τὴν διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος σωτη ρίαν· κἂν νύκτα εἴπῃς, κἂν ἡμέραν, κἂν ὥραν, κἂν στιγμὴν χρόνου, κἄν τι βραχύτατον. Πολλῷ δὲ δήπου εἰκὸς ἐπιτηδειότερον εἶναι τὸν οἰκειότερον. Τί δ' ἂν γένοιτο τῆς ἡμέρας τοῦ Πάσχα συγγενέστερον πρὸς τὸ βάπτισμα; Ἡ μὲν γὰρ ἡμέρα μνημόσυνόν ἐστιν ἀναστάσεως· τὸ δὲ βάπτισμα δύναμίς ἐστι πρὸς τὴν ἀνάστασιν. Ἐν τοίνυν τῇ ἀναστασίμῳ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τὴν χάριν ὑποδεξώμεθα. Διὰ τοῦτο πόῤ ῥωθεν ἡ Ἐκκλησία τοὺς ἑαυτῆς τροφίμους ὑψηλῷ κηρύγματι συγκαλεῖ, ἵν' οὓς πάλαι ὤδινεν, ἀπο κυήσῃ τότε, καὶ ἀπογαλακτίσασα αὐτοὺς τῶν λόγων τῆς κατηχήσεως, γεύσῃ τῆς στερεᾶς τῶν δογμάτων τροφῆς. Ἰωάννης ἐκήρυσσε βάπτισμα μετανοίας, καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία· Κύριος κηρύσσει βάπτισμα υἱοθεσίας· καὶ τίς τῶν εἰς αὐτὸν ἠλπικότων οὐχ ὑπακούσεται; Ἐκεῖνο εἰσαγωγικὸν τὸ βάπτισμα· τοῦτο τελειωτικόν. Ἐκεῖνο ἁμαρτίας ἀναχώρησις· τοῦτο οἰκείωσις πρὸς Θεόν. Ἑνὸς ἀν δρὸς ἦν Ἰωάννου τὸ κήρυγμα, καὶ πάντας εἷλκε πρὸς τὴν μετάνοιαν· σὺ δὲ, διὰ προφητῶν διδασκόμενος· Λούσασθε, καθαροὶ γίνεσθε· διὰ ψαλμῶν νουθετούμενος· Προσέλθετε πρὸς αὐτὸν, καὶ φωτίσθητε· δι' ἀποστόλων εὐαγγελιζόμενος· Μετανοήσατε, καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαστος ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν, καὶ λήψεσθε τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύμα τος· ὑπ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου προσλαμβανόμενος, λέγοντος· Δεῦτε πρὸς μὲ, πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι, κἀγὼ ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς (ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα σήμερον συνέδραμε πρὸς τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν)· ὀκνεῖς καὶ βουλεύῃ καὶ διαμέλλεις; Ἐκ νηπίου τὸν λόγον κατηχούμενος, οὔπω συνέθου τῇ ἀληθείᾳ; Πάντοτε μανθάνων, οὐδέπω ἦλθες πρὸς τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν; Πειραστὴς διὰ βίου, κατάσκοπος μέχρι γήρως, πότε γενήσῃ Χριστιανός; πότε γνωρίσομέν σε ὡς ἡμέτε ρον; Πέρυσι τὸν παρόντα καιρὸν ἐξεδέχου, νῦν πά λιν ἀναμένεις τὸν ἐπιόντα.
thought_title: Every moment is baptism's time, Easter most of all
orientation: Basil opens his homily by reworking Solomon's saying about times, arguing that the whole of human life is the season for baptism, and that Easter, as the day of resurrection, is the most fitting moment to receive it.
pass_a_gloss: Homily 13. Exhortation to holy baptism. The wise Solomon, dividing the seasons of the affairs in life, and marking off for each of the things that happen the suitable one, said: To all things there is a time, and a season for every matter: a season to give birth, and a season to die. But I, slightly altering the wise man's statement, would say as I proclaim to you the saving proclamation, that there is a season to die, and a season to be born. What is the reason for the change? Because the one who discusses the things that are in generation and corruption, following the bodily nature, placed birth before death (for it is impossible for one who has not first been born to have experience of death); but I, being about to make my discourse about the spiritual rebirth, place death before life. For through dying to the flesh there comes to us being born to the spirit, as the Lord also says: I will kill, and I will make alive. Let us die, then, in order that we may live. Let us kill the sinful nature, which is not able to be subject to the law of God, in order that the mindset of the spirit may be born strong in us, through which life and peace naturally come about. Let us be buried with Christ, who died for us, in order that we may also rise with him who procured for us the resurrection. One season, then, is suitable for different people for different things: one proper to sleep, and one proper to waking; one proper to war, and one proper to peace; but the season of baptism is the whole life of human beings. For neither is it possible for a body to live without breathing, nor for a soul to hold together without knowing the Creator. For ignorance of God is death of the soul. And the one who has not been baptized has not been enlightened. And without light neither does the eye see its own things, nor can the soul receive the contemplation of God. Every time, then, has a good opportunity for the salvation through baptism; whether you name night, whether day, whether an hour, whether an instant of time, whether anything very brief. But surely it is reasonable that the more fitting one is far more suitable. And what could be more akin to baptism than the day of Pascha? For the day is a memorial of resurrection; and baptism is a power for the resurrection. On the resurrection day, then, let us receive the grace of the resurrection. For this reason from early morning the Church summons her nurslings with a lofty proclamation, in order that those whom she long ago was in labor with, she may bring to birth then, and having weaned them from the words of catechesis, she may give them a taste of the solid food of the doctrines. John preached a baptism of repentance, and all Judea went out to him; the Lord preaches a baptism of adoption; and who of those who have hoped in him will not obey? That baptism was introductory; this one is perfecting. That one was a withdrawal from sin; this one is a drawing near to God. The proclamation was of one man, John, and it drew all to repentance; but you, being taught through the prophets: Wash, become clean; being admonished through the psalms: Come to him, and be enlightened; being evangelized through the apostles: Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the promise of the Holy Spirit; being invited by the Lord himself, who says: Come to me, all who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest (for all these things have come together today for the reading); do you hesitate and deliberate and keep delaying? Being catechized in the word from infancy, have you not yet come to agreement with the truth? Always learning, have you not yet come to knowledge? A tester through life, a spy until old age, when will you become a Christian? When will we recognize you as one of ours? Last year you awaited the present season, now again you wait for the coming one.

choices.why: Glossary term for the fleshly mindset hostile to God; keeps the Pauline sense of an active principle needing death.
Glossary term for baptism as adoption as God's child; preserves the legal-family metaphor Basil contrasts with John's repentance baptism.
Glossary term for spiritual regeneration; Basil explicitly contrasts it with bodily birth (γένεσις), so 'rebirth' keeps the parallel visible.
Keeps the light metaphor Basil immediately develops (eye, light, contemplation of God); 'enlightenment' is the glossary term for baptism.
Conveys the Church as mother nourishing her own; Basil pairs it with labor pains and weaning, so a maternal term is needed.
Renders the relational movement of being made God's own; contrasts with 'withdrawal from sin' for John's baptism.

pass_b_english: The wise Solomon, dividing up the times of life's affairs and setting aside the right moment for each thing that happens, said: "There is a time for everything, and a season for every matter: a time to be born, and a time to die" (Ecclesiastes 3:1-2). But I would alter the wise man's saying just a little, and proclaim to you the saving message: there is a time to die, and a time to be born.

Why this change? Because he was speaking about things that come into being and pass away, following bodily nature, and so he placed birth before death—for no one can experience death without first being born. But I am about to speak of spiritual rebirth, and so I place death before life. For by dying to the flesh we gain birth in the Spirit, as the Lord also says: "I kill, and I make alive" (Deuteronomy 32:39). Let us die, then, so that we may live. Let us put to death the sinful nature, which cannot submit to God's law, so that the mindset of the Spirit may grow strong in us—the mindset through which life and peace naturally come. Let us be buried with Christ, who died for us, so that we may also rise with Him who secured our resurrection.

Different times suit different things: there is a time for sleep and a time for waking, a time for war and a time for peace. But for baptism, the entire life of human beings is the time. A body cannot live without breathing, and a soul cannot hold together without knowing its Creator. Ignorance of God is the death of the soul. And the unbaptized person has not been enlightened. Without light, an eye cannot see what belongs to it, nor can a soul receive the contemplation of God.

Every moment, then, offers the opportunity for salvation through baptism—whether you name night or day, an hour or an instant, or the very briefest point of time. But surely the moment most closely related to baptism is the most fitting. What could be more akin to baptism than the day of Easter? That day is the memorial of the resurrection, and baptism is the power that leads to resurrection. On the day of resurrection, then, let us receive the grace of the resurrection. This is why the Church calls her nurslings together from afar with a loud proclamation, so that those for whom she long labored in birth she may bring forth on that day—and having weaned them from the words of instruction, she may give them a taste of the solid food of the teachings.

John the Baptist preached a baptism of repentance, and all Judea went out to him. The Lord preaches a baptism of adoption—and who among those who have hoped in Him will not obey? That baptism was introductory; this one brings to completion. That one was a withdrawal from sin; this one is a kinship with God. John the Baptist's preaching was that of one man, and it drew everyone to repentance. But you—taught through the prophets, "Wash yourselves; become clean" (Isaiah 1:16); admonished through the psalms, "Come to Him, and be enlightened" (Psalm 34:6); evangelized through the apostles, "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the promise of the Holy Spirit" (Acts 2:38); welcomed by the Lord Himself, who says, "Come to me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28)—for all these readings have come together today—do you still hesitate, deliberate, and keep delaying?

You have been instructed in the word since infancy, and you have not yet committed yourself to the truth? Always learning, and you have not yet come to knowledge? A tester your whole life, a spy until old age—when will you become a Christian? When will we recognize you as one of us? Last year you were waiting for this present season; now you are waiting again for the next one.

problems.why: οἰκείωσις means 'kinship,' 'adoption into the family,' or 'intimacy,' not merely 'drawing near.' The English weakens the claim of familial union.
problems.ruling: οἰκείωσις means kinship/familial union; 'drawing near' weakens the theological claim of intimate adoption.

problems.why: προσλαμβανόμενος means 'received,' 'taken in,' or 'welcomed,' not 'invited.' The English changes the sense from God's active reception to a mere invitation.
problems.ruling: προσλαμβανόμενος means 'received/welcomed,' not 'invited'; changes agency from God welcoming to God inviting.

edits.old: this one is a drawing near to God
edits.new: this one is a kinship with God

fixed: Changed 'a drawing near to God' to 'a kinship with God' to reflect οἰκείωσις πρὸς Θεόν as familial union, not mere proximity.
Changed 'invited by the Lord Himself' to 'welcomed by the Lord Himself' to reflect προσλαμβανόμενος as active reception, not invitation.

problems.why: LXX Psalm 33 becomes Psalm 34 in Hebrew numbering, but verse 6, not 5.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 33:6 (Hebrew 34:5) says 'come to Him'; verse reference should be 6, not 5.

fixed: Psalm 34:5 corrected to Psalm 34:6: LXX Psalm 33:6 corresponds to Hebrew Psalm 34:6.

last_rejected.ruling: LXX Psalm 33:6 equals Hebrew Psalm 34:5; citing English Bible 'Psalm 34:6' is off by one but standard English-verse referencing, not a major error.

last_rejected.ruling: τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος has the article; 'Spirit' is within normal range and fits the life-and-peace contrast with σαρκός.
